sections.content: How many people are "electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers"?

33,665 people

were counted on the census as "electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers maintain, service and repair domestic appliances, office machinery and electricity plant machinery, appliances and wiring.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers" there were more men than women (97.8% compared with 2.2%).

This means "electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled metal, electrical and electronic trades".

Men made up 97.8% and women made up 2.2% of "electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers" included:

  • construction and building trades (other)
  • welding trades
  • vehicle body builders and repairers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers", 15% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers" was 16 to 19 years.

  • parking and civil enforcement occupations
  • construction operatives (other)
  • glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers

We can look at who worked as "electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers", 8.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (89.9% compared with 10.1%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (87.8%) than self-employed (12.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
